one_liner: Newsletter platform for developers: write in Markdown, store posts in Git, and code blocks that render everywhere.
description: lettercraft is a newsletter platform built for people who write about code. Posts are Markdown files in a Git repository you own, code blocks come out syntax-highlighted and copyable in every major email client, and the subscriber list exports in one click with no lock-in. Publishing is a git push or a click — your choice.
target_user: Developers and technical writers running programming newsletters

icp.who: Developers, DevRel professionals, and technical bloggers with newsletters between 100 and 50,000 subscribers
icp.pain: Substack and beehiiv mangle code blocks and trap content in their editors, so technical writers fight their tools every single issue
icp.buying_trigger: One more issue shipped with broken code formatting, or a platform pricing change that makes lock-in feel dangerous

differentiators: Posts are Markdown files in a Git repo you own — write in your editor, publish with git push
Code blocks tested to render with syntax highlighting across 14 email clients
Full list and content export at any time; leaving is a git clone
proof_points: Code rendering verified across 14 email clients, with the test matrix published
Median send-to-inbox time under 60 seconds for lists under 10k

voice.sample_phrase: Write in Markdown. Publish with git push. Own every subscriber.

confidence.notes: Positioning and rendering claims are verifiable from the published test matrix. Growth numbers are beta-stage.
